editorialTake:
Luxury and jewellery brands are about to face a new kind of competition: not just for the sale, but for every moment after the sale. The evidence is clear. Amazon’s AI shopping assistant Rufus doubled its user base, showing shoppers now expect support and discovery well beyond checkout. Loop’s new AI-powered post-purchase tools are targeting the pain points luxury brands know too well, returns, fraud, and lost revenue, by turning these friction points into loyalty drivers. Meanwhile, live-shopping platform Whatnot’s integration with Shopify signals that the real action is shifting to how brands engage, entertain, and retain customers once the purchase is made, not just how they convert them in the first place.

This is not just a tech story. Zegna’s 7.4% revenue growth came from direct-to-consumer sales in the US, where operational control over the end-to-end experience is higher. Amazon’s claim to be the second-largest US grocer, with most sales online, shows how much of retail’s future will be won or lost in the invisible moments after the buy button. Even in jewellery, a Richmond store saw a 72% sales jump after new ownership rethought how to serve and re-engage existing customers, not just new ones.

Skeptics will say luxury is immune, that high-touch service cannot be automated or scaled by AI. But the bar for post-purchase experience is being raised for everyone, and luxury clients are already comparing their service to the best in any category, not just to other jewellers.

For the next quarter, I would put resources into the post-purchase journey: AI-powered consultations, seamless returns, clienteling tools that anticipate needs. The winners will be those who treat the transaction as the start of the relationship, not the end.
oneSentenceSummary: A surge of post-purchase AI solutions and live-shopping integrations signals that the battleground for value capture is shifting from the transaction to everything that follows it.
